prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five views show a narrow indoor space with walls or partitions on both sides and a person directly in front of the camera wearer; the person appears roughly 0.3–1 m away, while the visible background surfaces are approximately 1–3 m away. The person remains near the centre in frames 1–4, shifts slightly left and right as the camera turns, and is partly out of view toward the left in frame 5; small forms along the bottom edge are very near and heavily cropped. The depth map separates the side surfaces, central opening, and bottom-edge foreground more clearly than the dark, motion-blurred RGB, but it depicts the nearby person as very dark while some farther walls are bright, contradicting the stated brighter-is-nearer convention. Consequently, its relative depth ordering and metre estimates are unreliable, especially around the person, frame boundaries, and blurred edges.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies only one person, in frame 4, positioned slightly right of centre and extending below the bottom edge; the mask suggests that this person is close to and directly in front of the camera wearer, roughly 0.5–1 m away. No walls, floor, nearby objects, or additional people are segmented, so their distances, mutual spacing, and reachability cannot be established from this map. The detected person is partly cropped and the mask provides a clearer silhouette than the blurred RGB, but it does not resolve facial direction or whether the person looks toward the camera. The absence of masks in frames 1–3 and 5 despite a visible nearby person makes the temporal record highly unreliable and prevents a dependable description of approach, retreat, or turning.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely black across all five frames, so it provides no body or hand keypoints, facing direction, gaze direction, limb position, or arm-reach information. It therefore cannot spatially locate the person visible near the centre of the RGB frames, measure separation from the camera wearer or other surfaces, or show whether any body parts are occluded or outside the frame. The RGB suggests strong motion blur, close cropping, and repeated partial loss of the person at the image edges, all of which could account for the missing pose detections. No approach, retreat, turning, or relative movement can be inferred from this map itself.
